description: Rename a status page, move it to a new slug, publish and unpublish it, or change who may open it. An omitted field is left alone. Changing the slug moves the public URL and breaks existing links. access replaces the page's access settings and list whole: protected true makes it private to the listed domains and addresses (Team plan), and removes subscribers the list does not cover; protected false makes it public again and keeps the list. Not read-only; idempotent.

PageAccessArg.description:
Who may open a status page; the same shape as the REST `access` field. As a
write it replaces what is stored, whole.

protected.description:
Private when true: only people a way in lets through can open the
page: the addresses and domains in `rules`, by a code sent to their
email, or anyone with the page password. False makes it public again
and keeps the list and the password for next time.

rules.description:
Who can get an email code, up to 500 entries. Read back, these are
customer data.

session_days.description:
Keep a sign-in, by email or password, for 7, 30 or 90 days. Omit to
keep it until sign-out.

kind.description:
`domain` lets in every address at `value` (`example.com`); `address`
lets in one person (`name@example.com`).

PageEmailAccessArg.description: The emailed-code way in, and the passkeys that shortcut it.

enabled.description: Defaults to true. A private page needs it or the password.

passkeys_enabled.description: Let viewers save a passkey after an email sign-in. Defaults to true.

recheck_days.description:
Ask passkey viewers for an email code again after 30, 90 or 365 days.
Omit to never ask.

PagePasswordAccessArg.description:
The page password way in. The password itself never passes through here:
it is set in the app, the API or Terraform.

enabled.description:
Anyone with the page password can open the page. Turning it on needs
one already set; turning it off keeps it and signs out everyone who
came in with it.

inputSchema.description:
`update_status_page` argument. Every field but `slug` is optional; an
omitted field is left as it is.

access.description:
Replace who may open it: make it private, change its list, or make it
public again.

new_slug.description: New slug. Changing it moves the public URL and breaks existing links.

slug.description: The page to change, by its current slug.
